questions.text: Find the slope of the line through $(-3,\,2)$ and $(5,\,-6)$.
Find the inclination of a line whose slope is $-\sqrt{3}$.
The line through $(2,\,k)$ and $(4,\,7)$ is parallel to the line through $(0,\,1)$ and $(3,\,7)$. Find $k$.
Write the equation of the line with slope $\dfrac{2}{3}$ and $y$-intercept $-4$.
Find the intercepts that the line $4x-3y+24=0$ makes on the two axes.
Find $k$ if the line $kx+4y-7=0$ is perpendicular to the line $3x-2y+5=0$.
Find the distance of the point $(-2,\,3)$ from the line $12x-5y+1=0$.
Find the distance between the parallel lines $5x-12y+7=0$ and $10x-24y-13=0$.
Fill in the blanks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The slope of a line perpendicular to $2x+5y=9$ is ____________.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The equation of the line parallel to the $y$-axis, 3 units to its left, is ____________.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The line $3x+4y=12$ meets the $y$-axis at the point ____________.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The equation of the line through the origin with inclination $60^\circ$ is ____________.

parts.label: e
parts.text: The perpendicular distance of the origin from the line $3x-4y=10$ is ____________.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The slope of the line through $(a,\,b)$ and $(b,\,a)$, where $a\ne b$, is ____________.

questions.text: State True or False.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The lines $2x-3y=5$ and $6y=4x+1$ are parallel.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The slope of a vertical line is $0$.

parts.label: c
parts.text: The point $(2,\,-1)$ lies on the line $3x+2y=4$.

parts.label: d
parts.text: The $y$-intercept of the line $2x-5y+10=0$ is $-2$.

parts.label: e
parts.text: Two non-vertical lines with slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ are perpendicular when $m_1m_2=-1$.

parts.label: f
parts.text: The line $y=3$ is parallel to the $x$-axis.

Find the equation of the line through $(2,\,-3)$ that makes an angle of $135^\circ$ with the positive $x$-axis.
Find the equation of the line through $(-1,\,4)$ and $(3,\,-2)$. Write it in the form $ax+by+c=0$.
Find the equations of the lines whose $x$-intercept and $y$-intercept have sum $5$ and product $6$.
Without finding any equation, show that the line through $(2,\,5)$ and $(-1,\,3)$ is perpendicular to the line through $(0,\,0)$ and $(2,\,-3)$.
The vertices of a triangle are $A(2,\,3)$, $B(-1,\,0)$ and $C(4,\,-2)$. Find the equation of the median through $A$.
Find the image of the point $(1,\,2)$ in the line $2x-y+5=0$. (The line is the perpendicular bisector of the point and its image.)
Find the point where the lines $2x+3y=13$ and $5x-y=7$ meet. Then find the equation of the line through that point which is perpendicular to $3x-4y+1=0$.
Find the equations of the lines through $(3,\,-2)$ that make an angle of $60^\circ$ with the line $\sqrt{3}x+y=1$.
Find all values of $k$ for which the point $(k,\,2)$ is 4 units away from the line $3x+4y-6=0$.
$A(2,\,1)$ and $C(6,\,5)$ are opposite vertices of a square $ABCD$. Find the equation of the diagonal $BD$, and the coordinates of $B$ and $D$.
Find the equations of all lines that pass through $(2,\,3)$ and are at a distance of 2 units from the origin. (Do not forget a line that has no slope.)

The vertices $A(-2,\,3)$ and $B(2,\,1)$ of a rectangle $ABCD$ lie on the line $x+2y-4=0$. The vertex $C$ lies on the $x$-axis. Find the equations of the other three sides, and the coordinates of $C$ and $D$.
A line meets the $x$-axis at $A$ and the $y$-axis at $B$. The point $P(3,\,-4)$ divides $AB$ internally in the ratio $AP:PB=2:3$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the coordinates of $A$ and $B$.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equation of the line.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Find the length $AB$ and the area of $\triangle OAB$, where $O$ is the origin.

questions.text: The vertices of a triangle are $A(0,\,0)$, $B(6,\,0)$ and $C(2,\,4)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Find the equations of the altitudes from $A$ and from $C$, and hence the orthocentre.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Find the equations of the perpendicular bisectors of $AB$ and $AC$, and hence the circumcentre.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Check that the circumcentre is equally far from $A$, $B$ and $C$.

questions.text: A town planner draws a map on a coordinate grid, where 1 unit $=100$ m. The school is at the origin $O(0,\,0)$. A straight main road runs along the line $3x+4y=24$. The town wants a footpath from the school to the road that is as short as possible.

parts.label: i
parts.text: Find the points where the road crosses the $x$-axis and the $y$-axis. (1 mark)

parts.label: ii
parts.text: Find the slope of the road. (1 mark)

parts.label: iii
parts.text: Find the length of the shortest footpath from the school to the road, in metres. (2 marks)

orParts.label: iii
orParts.text: Find the equation of the footpath that meets the road at right angles, and the point where it meets the road. (2 marks)
